items.title: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
items.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

items.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
items.description: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

items.title: Ceuta: Documents show Spanish intelligence warned of crisis
items.description: Spain declassified documents that showed warnings issued a day before more than 70,000 migrants rushed the Ceuta border fence. Meanwhile, the EU announced funds to strengthen the border and return migrants to Morocco.

items.title: Europe's royalty pay respects to King Harald V in Norway
items.description: The Prince of Wales and three Nordic kings were among those who attended proceedings on Wednesday.

items.title: EU proposes more restrictions for Airbnb, holiday rentals
items.description: The European Union wants tighter rules on short-term rentals to tackle housing shortages in tourist hotspots.

items.title: Serbia dissolves parliament as snap elections called
items.description: Serbia will head to the polls in late October after President Aleksandar Vucic dissolved parliament following growing pressure from protesters demanding political change. However, Vucic plans to stand as a PM candidate.

items.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
items.description: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."
